clinician.final_diagnosis: primary acute aphthous genital ulcers in the setting of SARS-CoV-2
clinician.trajectory_summary: A 13-year-old girl developed severe vulvar ulceration, edema, and pain following systemic symptoms and confirmed COVID-19 infection. Physical exam revealed multiple shallow, sharply demarcated vulvar ulcers with exudate and eschar. Infectious causes HSV, EBV, syphilis, and HIV were excluded by negative testing, as were Behcet’s syndrome markers. The patient was hospitalized for pain control and treated with a 14-day oral steroid course and topical analgesics, resulting in decreased edema but persistent ulcers initially. Within six weeks, ulceration and edema resolved but labial adhesions developed, necessitating surgical lysis. Postoperative evaluation showed normal anatomy and pain resolution, confirming diagnosis and clinical course consistent with primary acute aphthous genital ulcers in the context of SARS-CoV-2 infection.
